Which of the following classical dance forms is associated with Hindustani Classical Music?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India and originated in North India.**
 
• The dance form has its roots in the Mughal era and is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful hand movements, and storytelling through facial expressions.
 
• Kathak is closely associated with Hindustani classical music and is often performed to the accompaniment of tabla, sarangi, and sitar.
 
• The nineteenth century saw the **golden age of Kathak under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Oudh.**
 
• He established the **Lucknow Gharana with its strong accent on bhava, the expression of moods and emotions.**
 
• The **Jaipur Gharana is known for its layakari or rhythmic virtuosity and the Benaras Gharana is another prominent school of Kathak dance**.
 
• The technique of movement in Kathak is unique.
 
• Today, Kathak has **emerged as a distinct dance form**.
 
• Being the only classical dance of India having links with Muslim culture, it represents a unique synthesis of Hindu and Muslim genius in art.
 
• **Further, Kathak is the only form of classical dance wedded to Hindustani or North Indian music.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​__Kathak dance is a combination of music, dance, and narrative. 
 
• The name Kathak is derived from the Sanskrit word *katha* meaning story.
 
• This dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathaks, or storytellers.
 
• The present-day Kathak dance mainly depends on the medieval period *Ras Lila*, a local dance in the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an NGO involved in microfinance-related activities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD in Mumbai.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **NGO stands for Non-Governmental Organization,** which is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. NGOs are usually involved in social, cultural, and environmental activities to promote social welfare.
 
• **Microfinance is a financial service **provided to low-income individuals or groups who do not have access to traditional banking services. Microfinance institutions provide small loans, savings, insurance, and other financial services to help people improve their livelihoods.
 
• **MYRADA in Bangalore is an NGO** that works in the areas of rural development, natural resource management, and microfinance. SEWA in Ahmedabad is another NGO that provides microfinance services to women entrepreneurs. ADITHI in Patna is an NGO that works for the empowerment of women and children through education, health, and livelihood programs.
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) **is a development bank that provides financial and technical assistance to rural areas in India. While NABARD supports microfinance institutions and self-help groups, it is not an NGO as it is a government-owned institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A large amount of loan is not a basic principle of micro-financial institutions in India.
 
• The functions of Microfinance institutions are:
 
 
• Maintain macroeconomic stability.
 
• Avoid interest-rate caps.
 
• Refrain from distorting the market with unsustainable subsidized.
 
• High-delinquency loan programs.
 
 
 
• MFIs are financial companies that provide small loans to people who do not have any access to banking facilities.
 
• The definition of “small loans” varies between countries. In India, all loans that are below Rs. 1 lakh can be considered as microloans.
 
• Various types of institutions offer microfinance:
 
 
• ​Credit unions.
 
• Commercial banks.

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap?

i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic.

iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.

options.text: Only Statements i and ii are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement iii is correct.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A liquidity trap is a situation where monetary policy becomes ineffective due to the zero lower bound on interest rates.**
 
• **​**Liquidity trap:
 
• A liquidity trap refers to a situation in which an increase in the money supply does not result in a fall in the interest rate but merely in addition to idle balances the interest elasticity of demand for money becomes infinite.
 
• Under normal conditions, an increase in money supply, resulting in excess cash balances, would cause an increase in bond prices, as individuals sought to acquire assets in exchange for money, and a corresponding fall in interest rates.
 
• The horizontal portion of the liquidity preference curve is referred to as the liquidity trap.
 
• In this portion of the curve, the demand for money is infinitely elastic with respect to the interest rate.
 
• Re­ductions in the interest rate, in this portion only, increase people’s desire to hold cash balances
 
• Statement 3 is correct as It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.
 
• In a liquidity trap, people prefer holding money regardless of the interest rate because they expect that the return on other assets will not be better. Therefore, the demand for money is infinitely elastic (it does not change with interest rates), and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly horizontal or elastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__"**

Speculative Demand for Money: In a liquidity trap, speculative demand for money is actually infinitely elastic, not inelastic. This means that people are willing to hold an unlimited amount of money at a particular low interest rate, because they expect interest rates to rise in the future, which would cause bond prices to fall.

 
 
• 
 
Liquidity Preference Curve: The curve becomes perfectly elastic (horizontal) at the liquidity trap, indicating that changes in the money supply will not affect interest rates because people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds.

 Thus, this statement is incorrect because it incorrectly describes speculative demand for money as infinitely inelastic

**Photoelectric effect:**

__
 
• **The phenomenon in which light energy forces a metal surface to release electrons is called the photoelectric effect.**
 
• When the light hits, it shows the particle theory of light, and light is defined as a stream of photons or energy packets.
 
• The other phenomena such as interference, diffraction, and polarization can only be explained when the light is treated as a wave wherein the photoelectric effect, **line spectra, and the production and scattering of x-rays demonstrate the particle nature of light.**

**Properties of Lightwaves:**

 
• Not have any charge or we can say that they are neutral.
 
• Propagate as a transverse wave with both wave and particle nature.
 
• **They move with a velocity the same as that of light i.e. 3 × 10⁸ m/s.**
 
• It contains energy and it also contains momentum.
 
• They can travel in a vacuum and always travel in a straight line.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• However, it is not directly related to the photoelectric effect.
 
 
 
• ** Wave nature refers** to the fact that light can exhibit interference and diffraction patterns, similar to water waves or sound waves.
 
 
• This is important in many areas of physics,** but again, not directly relevant to the photoelectric effect.**
